description: The PYthoN General UnIt Test geNerator is a test-generation tool for Python

summary.one_liner: Pynguin is a command-line tool that automatically generates unit tests for Python modules, aimed at general-purpose dynamically typed code.
summary.what_it_does: Pynguin takes a Python module under test and automatically produces unit tests for it, written to an output directory. It is run from the command line as `pynguin`, with options such as a project path, output path, and module name. The README says it can use a whole-suite test generation approach. It is described as the first tool of its kind for generating unit tests for general Python programs, a gap the README says existed for dynamically typed languages. The README explicitly warns that Pynguin executes the module under test, so it should be run in an isolated environment such as a Docker container. It is described as a research prototype, not intended for production use.
use_cases: automatically generate unit tests for a Python module
bootstrap a test suite for legacy Python code
exploring coverage of untested Python functions
generating regression tests for a Python project
how_to_run: Install Python 3.10 or newer (3.11 to 3.15 experimental)
Activate the virtual environment where Pynguin is installed
notable: Automatic unit test generation for dynamically typed Python code
Command-line interface with whole-suite generation option
Developed at the University of Passau Chair of Software Engineering II
Originally LGPL until version 0.29.0, MIT from version 0.30.0
caveats: Executes the module under test, which can cause serious harm; run it in an isolated environment such as Docker
Described as a research prototype, not tailored for production use
Requires Python 3.10 or newer; newer Python versions are only experimentally supported
